details.body: The depth-weighted average porosity in `effective_substrate_porosity` (systems/substrate.rs:127-139) may significantly overestimate O₂ penetration when a low-porosity top layer (e.g., fine sand, porosity 0.35) sits above a high-porosity deep layer (e.g., lava rock, porosity 0.55). In reality, the top layer's porosity is the rate-limiting bottleneck for surface-to-depth O₂ diffusion. The weighted average dilutes this constraint with the deeper layer's porosity, producing a D_eff that's too high. Consider using the porosity of the topmost layer (or the layer at the penetration boundary) instead of the depth-weighted average across the full stack, or document this as a known limitation with a TODO for heterogeneous-stack correction.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/substrate.rs:81-124` does not include microfauna in `estimate_substrate_o2_demand_rate()`. The new redox boundary is therefore unaffected by `MicrofaunaState`, even though the bead defines substrate O2 demand as coming from decomposers, roots, and microfauna. In detritivore-heavy tanks this will overestimate `o2_penetration_depth_cm` and understate the suboxic volume that downstream denitrification/root-zone work consumes.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/substrate.rs:127-139` computes `D_eff` from a depth-weighted average porosity across the entire stacked bed. For heterogeneous substrates, that lets deep high-porosity layers make the surface diffusion path look easier than it is. A thin low-porosity cap over coarse lower media will therefore produce an oxic boundary that is too deep, even though oxygen has to traverse the cap first.

In `molt_cycle` (shrimp.rs ~lines 496-506), when multiple stages resolve on the same tick with different outcomes (some fail, some succeed), `last_molt_success` is unconditionally set to `false` by the failure branch but the `failed_molt_accum` accumulator net-decreases by 0.05 (increases 0.3 from failure, then decreases 0.35 from success). This creates an inconsistency: `last_molt_success` is read downstream as a sub-adult maturation gate (line 849), so a juvenile molt failure on the same tick as an adult molt success will block sub-adult maturation despite the accumulator showing improvement. Fix: either resolve per-stage outcomes independently (track `last_molt_success` per stage, use the sub-adult's own result for its maturation gate), or ensure the accumulator and boolean agree (e.g., only apply the success decrement to the accumulator when `!any_failed`).

In `estimate_substrate_microfauna_o2_demand_mg_per_s` (substrate.rs line 188), the detritus daily consumption fraction `0.01` is a magic constant not backed by any `process_params` field: `substrate_detritus_consumed_g = fine_detritus_g_total * 0.01 * population_index * substrate_fraction`. Unlike the periphyton consumption fraction which reads from `process_params.microfauna_periphyton_consumption`, this value is hardcoded and cannot be tuned via configuration. Extract it to a named constant with a documentation comment explaining the value's provenance, or add it to `ProcessParams` alongside the periphyton consumption parameter.

Legacy timer migration now runs on brand-new states, not just old saves. `StageCohort` still defaults `molt_timer_days` to `0.0` and `AnimalState::default()` still seeds `inter_molt_timer_days` to `14.0` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:105-114`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:594-617`). On the first daily tick, the migration branch in `molt_cycle` copies that legacy timer into every stage timer whenever they are all zero (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:409-419`). That means a fresh juvenile cohort starts effectively 14 days into a 14-day cycle and can molt immediately, while adults start halfway through their 28-day cycle. The new per-stage cadence therefore does not actually start cleanly for fresh simulations.

The per-stage molt loop undercounts failure pressure whenever multiple stages resolve on the same day. Default intervals are 14/21/28 days (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:433-438`), so overlaps are guaranteed at days 42 and 84, but the accumulator logic only tracks `any_failed`/`any_succeeded` booleans (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:440-442`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:467-472`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:495-506`). Two or three failed stages still add only one `+0.3`, and a mixed day (one failure plus one success) actually lowers `failed_molt_accum` because both branches run. That makes mortality pressure weakest exactly on the days when more of the population is molting.

The new shrimp preset knobs added in `crates/tank_data/data/shrimp/neocaridina_davidi.toml:23-27` are currently dead configuration. `ShrimpPreset` does not declare `ca_min_mg_per_l`, `mg_min_mg_per_l`, `juvenile_molt_interval_days`, `sub_adult_molt_interval_days`, or `molt_success_threshold` (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:430-472`), its metadata helpers do not recognize those names (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:658-733`), and `shrimp_preset_to_params` never copies them into `ShrimpRuntimeParams` (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:746-799`). Because TOML deserialization here ignores unknown keys, the file still loads but silently drops all five values.

details.message: remediation exhausted at cycle 4; maximum supported cycles is 3
